trust_decision.summary: UPF/SGW-U data-plane code decides whether a failed PFCP Session Report Request (transaction pool exhausted by peer-driven GTP-U/downlink traffic, builder or update_tx failure) is fatal: at the pinned commit every caller wraps the send in ogs_assert(OGS_OK == ...), and the send function leaks its local xact on build/update_tx failure.

landing_point.why: Summary names 'GTP-U Receive Path gtp-path.c' and ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create; the UPF _gtpv1_u_recv_one Error-Indication branch is the first assert around upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request on the GTP-U receive path.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/sgwu/gtp-path.c:176-177 and src/sgwu/gtp-path.c:272-273 (separate SGW-U daemon with its own send helper src/sgwu/pfcp-path.c:348-384); also src/upf/context.c:939-940, a timer callback in the session-context file rather than any gtp-path receive path

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The summary names the UPF GTP-U receive path; SGW-U is a separate EPC-only daemon and the URR timer callback in context.c is not a packet receive path, so a solver can argue both are a different component or 'not attacker-driven'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Buffering and the one-time Downlink Data Report must keep working: the packet is still buffered or forwarded and URR accounting/timer re-arm (context.c:824, :943) must still run after a failed report. An over-broad fix that drops the packet, removes the session, or returns early before upf_sess_urr_acc_timers_setup breaks paging and usage reporting.

UE-to-UE looped G-PDU into a buffering downlink FAR (UPF)
N6 downlink IP packet from TUN into a buffering FAR (UPF)
volume threshold/quota crossing in URR accounting
failure kinds in the helper: xact pool exhausted, report build failure, xact_update_tx failure

O7_producer.where: Failure originates in lib/pfcp/xact.c:77-81 (pool allocation returning NULL), not in a schema/serializer/cache producer

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Downstream consumer in another NF; the input is a PFCP report, not a GTP-U packet

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: SMF is control plane and the ei_deactivation flags (n4-handler.c:1911-1923) look like they already de-duplicate repeats

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An Error-Indication-on-unknown-TEID path that also emits a report via an asserted send
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same function already chooses between sending an Error Indication and a report; a maintainer adding a 'report unknown TEID to SMF' feature would copy the asserted pattern used elsewhere in the file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An asserted response send whose helper (src/upf/pfcp-path.c:239-250) leaks its buffer or xact on build failure, in the same style as the report helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The response helpers already share the report helper's build/update_tx error structure without cleanup.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A buffered-packet overflow notification that triggers a further report per dropped packet
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The buffering limit branch already exists, and a 'buffer full' report is a plausible feature request.

O9_family: Resource exhaustion / reachable assertion on allocation failure (CWE-400/770/617): PFCP transaction pool exhausted by traffic-driven Session Report Requests, which aborts UPF/SGW-U; also an xact leak on error paths

O10_build.toolchain: meson + ninja, gcc; deps libsctp, libgnutls, libgcrypt, libidn, libyaml, libmicrohttpd, libnghttp2, libtalloc, mongo-c (for other NFs)
services: TUN device (/dev/net/tun) for UPF/SGW-U data plane
MongoDB for the project's integration tests (tests/)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/ integration suites (attach, 5gc, etc.) drive full NF stacks and need MongoDB plus SCTP; no unit test targets this report-failure path, and the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the assert only at the UPF Error-Indication site (or raise the xact pool size), leaving the SGW-U copy, the URR context.c sites and the xact leak in the send helper untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Heartbeat sends asserted in src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:172 and src/sgwu/pfcp-sm.c:167 are timer-driven, not GTP-U-driven; not pursued.
The response-send helpers (src/upf/pfcp-path.c:239-250 and sgwu equivalents) are PFCP-request-driven and asserted in n4-handler.c/sxa-handler.c; this is a different input surface.
unverified: Whether a UPF build/test harness can run without a TUN device (UPF opens TUN at startup) was not checked; this may require NET_ADMIN or the tun module in the test environment.

Whether the SGW-C/SMF O8 routes can realistically exhaust their GTP/PFCP xact pools under report floods (rate depends on the one-report-per-buffer-start logic at lib/pfcp/handler.c:345-349 and on Error Indication frequency) was not checked.
